hypothesis: A 32x33 padded shared tile with 8x32 threads, each owning four adjacent input and output values, may improve on the prior scalar-ownership variants by using aligned 16-byte global transfers and fewer per-element global instructions. Integer bit-pattern transfers avoid floating-point arithmetic. The supplied measurements make XOR-swizzled scalar ownership a slightly faster comparison point than padded scalar ownership, but neither result predicts this vectorized variant's performance.
notes: No commands were run. The vector accesses assume the input and output pointers are suitably aligned for uint4; CUDA allocation bases and offsets for these row and tile sizes meet that alignment. transformations: Replace the naive transpose kernel with a single-pass 32x32 shared-memory tile using an 8x32 block; each thread owns four adjacent input columns and four transposed output elements.
Keep the 32x33 padded shared layout, stage values as unsigned 32-bit patterns, and use aligned uint4 global loads and stores without floating-point arithmetic.
Preserve the run entry point, add no allocation, and tile the full n-by-n matrix for positive n multiples of 32.
